target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures concern the FASB November 2023 standard on significant expense disclosures in operating segments. D068 states the company is evaluating the impact before adoption, while D061 confirms adoption in FY2025. Evidence: D068 (nvda_2024_8_P066_S001, S002, S003), D061 (nvda_2025_8_P066_S001, S002).

The 2024 disclosure (D068) identifies a specific FASB standard issued in November 2023 requiring additional disclosures about significant expenses in operating segments, effective for FY2025. The 2025 disclosure (D063) identifies a different FASB standard issued in November 2024 requiring disclosures of specific expense components (inventory, compensation, depreciation, etc.), effective for FY2028. These are two distinct accounting standards with different issuance dates, subjects (operating segments vs. specific expense captions), and effective dates. They do not share the same specific subject.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU 2023-07 on Segment Reporting
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company adopted FASB ASU 2023-07 in the fourth quarter of 2024 to enhance disclosures about significant segment expenses, as this standard was effective for fiscal year 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD discuss the adoption of FASB ASU 2023-07 regarding segment expense disclosures. However, their status differs materially: AMD adopted the standard in Q4 2024 for fiscal year 2024, whereas NVDA is still evaluating the impact for the future fiscal year 2025. AMD states, 'The Company adopted this standard in the fourth quarter of 2024,' while NVDA notes, 'We are currently evaluating the impact of this standard on our Consolidated Financial Statements.'

The Company adopted this standard in the fourth quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of ASU 2023-07 on Segment Disclosures
comparisons.peer_summary: In November 2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-07, which enhances disclosures regarding significant segment expenses; this standard is effective for annual reporting in 2025 on a retrospective basis and will impact the company's disclosures without affecting its financial statements.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the same FASB standard (ASU 2023-07) and its effective timing, but differ in the reporting year and current action. Both identify the standard as effective for annual reporting in 2025 retrospectively. MU confirms, 'This standard will impact our disclosures and will not impact our financial statements,' while NVDA remains in the evaluation phase: 'We are currently evaluating the impact of this standard on our Consolidated Financial Statements.'

sentences.text: In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board, or FASB, issued a new accounting standard to provide for additional disclosures about significant expenses in operating segments.
The standard is effective for our annual reporting for fiscal year 2025 and for interim period reporting starting in fiscal year 2026 retrospectively.
We are currently evaluating the impact of this standard on our Consolidated Financial Statements.
In November 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU") 2023-07 (ASC Topic 280), Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures.
This ASU is effective for our annual reporting for 2025 on a retrospective basis.
This standard will impact our disclosures and will not impact our financial statements.
